# The Paradox of the Cheap Part: Why Appliance Repair Is Hard

There's a moment familiar to anyone who has attempted to fix a household appliance: you've identified the broken component, looked it up online, and discovered it costs $12.95. Yet the repair quote from a professional is $250, or the DIY project consumes an entire weekend and ends in frustration. The part was cheap; the repair was not. This gap between the cost of a component and the cost of fixing it is one of the most underappreciated realities of modern consumer life. To understand it, we can follow a fictional but entirely typical case: a washing machine whose drain pump has failed.

## The Diagnosis Problem
